* Lead the day-to-day manufacturing function as we transition from in-house builds to volume production with a contract manufacturer (CM).

* Demonstrated success building and mentoring technical teams.
* Highly motivated teammate with excellent oral and written communication skills.
* Enjoy working in a fast-paced, collaborative, and dynamic start-up environment as part of a small team.
* Willing to occasionally travel.
* Must have and maintain US work authorization.

* Experience with MES, SPC, or similar production tracking systems.
* Background in robotics or complex electromechanical hardware.
* Familiarity with regulatory requirements and certifications (CE, UL, ISO9001, ISO13485).
* Demonstrated ability to drive cost, yield, and quality improvements in manufacturing.
* Advanced degree in engineering, operations, or related field.

Why join GroupeSTAHL?

We value work/life balance.As a family-owned business, we know our work family is just one aspect of life. We offer flexibility in the workplace to accommodate life outside of work. We offer generous PTO packages and opportunity to earn additional time off throughout the year.

We take health and wellness seriously.We offer comprehensive benefits packages with low premiums and front-end deductibles. Contribute pre-tax dollars to your FSA or HSA accounts. Earn additional PTO by participating in healthy activities!

We believe in making a difference (and having fun while doing it).Whether we’re eating hot dogs to celebrate Coney Day, or playing hockey with Detroit Red Wings Alumni to raise money for Michigan Disabled Veterans. We’re a family-owned company who has family-friendly fun year ‘round! We’re all about having fun and making a difference.

Need more reasons to join GroupeSTAHL? Read more about other benefits and perks HERE!

What we do:GroupeSTAHL is a leading international manufacturer, distributor and direct supplier in the field of custom textile printing.

### What you'll be doing:

Stahls' is seeking a Senior Director of Operations to lead day-to-day manufacturing and operational performance across its Chesterfield, MI-based decoration facilities. This role owns production output, quality, safety, and continuous improvement across the Chesterfield, MI campus and serves as the senior operational leader on the ground for this facility cluster. The Senior Director of Operations partners closely with the Executive Vice President of Manufacturing and Operations to translate enterprise-wide operational strategy into plant-level execution, and represents Chesterfield, MI operations in cross-divisional planning.

### KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Operational Leadership

* Own daily production performance across the Chesterfield (SF1, VCF) facilities, including throughput, on-time delivery, and capacity utilization
* Set and drive plant-level goals that ladder up to enterprise operational targets set by the Executive Vice President of Manufacturing and Operations
* Lead, coach, and develop Plant Managers and department leaders across the Chesterfield, MI facility cluster

Quality & Safety

* Champion a strong safety culture and ensure compliance with all workplace safety standards across facilities
* Own quality performance, root-cause analysis, and corrective action for production defects and customer complaints

Continuous Improvement

* Drive lean manufacturing and continuous improvement initiatives to reduce waste, improve first-pass yield, and lower cost per unit
* Identify and lead capital equipment and process improvement projects, partnering with the Executive Vice President of Manufacturing and Operations on capital planning and justification

Cross-Functional & Strategic Coordination

* Partner with Supply Chain, Quality, HR, and Customer Service leaders to resolve cross-functional operational issues
* Represent Chesterfield operations in enterprise-wide planning, staffing, and reporting initiatives led by the Executive Vice President of Manufacturing and Operations

People Leadership

* Build and maintain a strong bench of operations talent, including hiring, retention, and succession planning across the facility cluster
* Establish clear performance standards and accountability for production teams

### QUALIFICATIONS & EXPERIENCE

* Bachelor's degree in Operations Management, Industrial Engineering, Business, or a related field; MBA a plus
* 10+ years of progressive manufacturing or production operations leadership experience, including multi-site or multi-shift responsibility
* Prior experience in a Director of Operations, or senior Plant Manager role, ideally in apparel decoration, textiles, printing, or a related light-manufacturing environment
* Demonstrated track record improving safety, quality, on-time delivery, and cost performance in a production setting
* Working knowledge of lean manufacturing, Six Sigma, or other continuous improvement methodologies
* Strong financial acumen, including experience managing plant P&L, labor planning, and capital expenditure justification
* Proven ability to lead, develop, and hold accountable a team of plant managers and front-line supervisors
* Excellent communication skills, with the ability to partner effectively with executive leadership and cross-functional peers
* Comfortable operating in a fast-paced, hands-on manufacturing environment with regular presence on the plant floor

### LOCATION, TRAVEL & WORK ENVIRONMENT

This position is based on-site at the Chesterfield, Michigan campus. This is a hands-on manufacturing leadership role: the Senior Director of Operations is expected to spend significant time on the plant floor, not primarily behind a desk.

Occasional travel (estimated 10%) may be required for site visits to other Stahls' facilities, vendor or customer visits, or company leadership meetings.

Seeking a Vice President, Operations to lead the performance and development of our U.S. manufacturing and supply-chain footprint and to help build the operating capability required for the next stage of growth.

Reporting directly to the President, this role will be a key member of the Americas Executive Leadership Team with accountability for multi-site operational performance, continuous improvement, supply-chain resilience, quality, capacity and operational integration.

The Role

The VP Operations will lead Americas’ operational value-creation agenda, with particular focus on:

- Multi-site operational performance and SQDIP management
- Operational Excellence, Lean and continuous improvement
- Manufacturing productivity, throughput and margin expansion
- Strategic sourcing, supply-chain resilience and SIOP
- Capacity, capital and footprint optimization
- Quality, compliance and production discipline
- New Product Introduction (NPI), production readiness & technology transfer
- Operational integration of acquisitions and new capabilities
- Leadership capability and consistent operating practices across sites
- The role will improve the performance of today’s operations while building scalable, consistent capabilities

- Own site and network performance across Safety, Quality, Delivery, Inventory and Productivity (SQDIP), with clear targets, operating reviews and accountability for corrective action.
- Develop and deploy a common Operational Excellence system, embedding Lean, continuous improvement, standard work, visual management and structured problem solving across the U.S. footprint.

- Partner with Engineering & Product to ensure robust NPI, Design for Manufacturability, production readiness and clean handoff of new technologies and products into U.S. operations.

- Build strong site leadership, manufacturing, quality, supply-chain and continuous‑improvement capability, creating common standards and sharing best practice across locations.
- Provide clear, fact‑based operational reporting to the President and Executive Leadership Team, identifying risks early and maintaining pace on recovery and value‑creation actions.

Transformation will coordinate the enterprise program and cross‑functional dependencies; Operational Excellence will own execution and sustained embedding within the operating sites.
- With Product & Technology, the role will ensure innovation and technical programs move effectively from development into repeatable, high‑quality production, with common readiness measures, clear handoffs and strong cross‑functional execution.
- The role will also partner closely with Business Development, People & Culture, Finance, IT and other functions to ensure operations can support customer commitments, growth plans, workforce requirements and Group standards.

- Building high‑performing site leadership teams and creating consistency across multiple facilities
- Strong financial literacy, KPI management and executive communication

Experience in aerospace, defense, life‑support/PPE, advanced manufacturing, engineered products or other complex industrial environments would be highly valued. U.S. defense‑sector experience is strongly advantageous.

* Coordinate schedule integration across engineering, operations, safety basis, licensing, supply chain, construction, and quality.
* Lead schedule risk analysis, critical path modeling, resource planning, and recovery strategies.

* Oversee variance analysis, corrective-action plans, performance metrics, and leadership reporting for BWXT and federal customers.
* Lead Integrated Baseline Reviews (IBRs), EO executive Monthly Progress Reviews (MPR), and customer reporting cycles.
 ### Risk & Opportunity Management * Develop EO’s enterprise risk framework including risk registers, burn‑down tracking, mitigation planning, and root‑cause analysis.
* Oversee quantification of technical, schedule, cost, regulatory, and supply chain risks.
* Drive cross-functional risk ownership and monthly risk summits across EO.
 ### Cross Functional Technical Integration * Coordinate deeply with engineering, operations, nuclear safety, security, quality, and supply chain to ensure alignment of program execution.
* Maintain configuration control of technical baselines across design, manufacturing, and facility deployments.
 ### Regulatory & Customer Alignment * Support licensing schedules, readiness assessments, NRC interactions, DOE/NNSA data calls, audits, and performance reviews.
* Ensure PMO documentation meets DOE, NRC, QA, and BWXT governance requirements.
 ### Leadership, Culture, and Organizational Development * Build EO’s PMO team, including Program Controllers, Master Schedulers, Risk Managers, and Project Managers.
* Mentor PM1–PM5 personnel and develop professional pathways for PMO staff.
* Establish a culture of transparency, disciplined execution, and mission-first alignment.

* Minimum 12+ years leading large-scale PMO, program management, or project controls organizations.
* Demonstrated success managing federal programs >$250M+ (preferred >$1B).
* Proven experience implementing integrated master schedules and enterprise program controls.
* Experience with DOE or NNSA programs, NRC licensing environments, nuclear manufacturing, defense programs, or highly regulated industries.

* An inclusive atmosphere that celebrates new perspectives and supports collaboration between different generations.
* The chance to be part of a mission-driven organization making a positive impact on the future of energy.

San Carlos, CA

## About 1X

We’re building humanoid robots that work in any space humans exist with the mission to create an abundance of labor. Simple, but it’s not.

To do this right, we have to solve robotics, AI, software, hardware, manufacturing and operations at the same time, at scale, in a form factor that has to be safe. If you’re inspired by this, you’ll thrive here. We’ve been at this since 2014 and we’re at the point where the hard problems are behind us and the hard work is in front of us.

NEO is our flagship - a general purpose robot designed to move, learn, and operate in the real world alongside real people. We’re not demoing it, we're shipping it. We’re excited to meet you, if this excites you.

If you’ve spent your career working on problems that matter and want to see them actually reach the world - this is that moment. We’re scaling, we’re hiring with intention, and we need people who want to build something that will genuinely change how humans spend their time safely creating abundance for all.

## About the Team

The Quality Engineering team enables 1X to scale complex humanoid robot hardware with speed, confidence, and strong manufacturing discipline. We partner across Design Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Supply Chain, Software, and Operations to build quality into the product and production system from the beginning.

As we scale NEO, the team owns quality across new product introduction, production, incoming inspection, MRB, and quality systems. Our goal is to solve quality problems at the source while building practical systems that improve product reliability without slowing engineering or production.

## Your Charter

Build and lead a high-performing Quality Engineering organization that establishes quality from product design through production. You will own quality planning, manufacturing controls, production quality, incoming inspection, MRB, and quality system development while driving technical problem-solving across critical robot systems.

Your charter is to translate design intent into robust manufacturing and inspection controls, resolve quality issues at their source, and build a scalable quality organization that supports 1X’s path to production.

## Key Outcomes

* Build and lead the Quality Engineering organization, including Quality Engineers and the Quality Technician Supervisor, with clear ownership across NPI, production quality, incoming inspection, MRB, and quality systems.
* Establish quality planning for new products by translating design requirements into measurable manufacturing controls, inspection strategies, control plans, and acceptance criteria.
* Lead PFMEA and control plan development with Design and Manufacturing Engineering to identify critical risks and establish effective prevention, detection, and reaction controls.
* Drive timely resolution of significant production and incoming quality issues through containment, structured root cause analysis, corrective action, and verification of durable fixes.
* Develop and improve practical Quality Management Systems and MRB processes that establish traceability, disciplined decision-making, and useful quality data without unnecessary bureaucracy.
* Partner with Design, Manufacturing, Software, Supply Chain, and Operations to improve product and process quality across motors, batteries, electronics, structural assemblies, and other critical robot systems.
* Use inspection results, metrology, defect trends, and production feedback to prioritize systemic improvements, communicate quality performance to leadership, and raise the quality bar as production scales.

## Key Competencies

* Technical and hands-on quality engineering leader who can build an organization while remaining close to complex manufacturing and product quality problems.
* Strong expertise in NPI quality planning, PFMEA, control plans, inspection strategies, and manufacturing process controls.
* Proven ability to lead structured problem-solving, containment, root cause analysis, and corrective action across cross-functional engineering and production teams.
* Strong understanding of electromechanical hardware, including motors, batteries, electronics, and structural components, and the quality controls used to manufacture and inspect them.
* First-principles approach to building quality systems that are practical, scalable, and aligned with engineering and production needs.
* Effective cross-functional leader who can influence Design Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Supply Chain, Software, Operations, and senior leadership.
* Strong operational judgment, ownership, and ability to prioritize quality risks in a fast-moving production environment.

## Minimum Requirements

* 5+ years of experience in a Quality Engineering management role within a complex hardware, electromechanical, automotive, aerospace, robotics, or similarly demanding manufacturing environment.
* Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical, Electrical, Manufacturing, Materials, or a related engineering discipline.
* Demonstrated experience leading Quality Engineers and technical quality teams through new product introduction and production ramp.
* Strong technical experience with manufacturing quality controls for complex electromechanical hardware, including inspection, metrology, and process validation.
* Proven experience developing and implementing control plans, PFMEA, inspection strategies, and corrective action processes.
* Deep experience with structured problem-solving, root cause analysis, and building practical quality systems.
* Strong cross-functional leadership and communication skills, with the ability to work directly with engineering, supply chain, operations, and senior leadership.

## Preferred Skills

* Experience scaling quality engineering organizations and systems through rapid production growth or high-rate NPI.
* Experience in robotics, electric vehicles, consumer electronics, or other vertically integrated electromechanical products.
* Experience developing or improving MRB, incoming inspection, metrology, and production quality operating systems.
* Familiarity with statistical quality methods, process capability, measurement system analysis, and data-driven quality reporting.
* Experience working across motors, batteries, electronics, structural assemblies, and other complex hardware systems.
* Experience building quality systems from first principles in a startup or rapidly scaling manufacturing environment.

## What does a successful 1X Team Member look like?

Team members at 1X who thrive here are builders. They move fast, own their work completely, and treat time like it’s the one thing you can’t get back - because it is. Are you inspired by challenging the status quo? Do you thrive in collaborative environments that drive results? If so, Gates could be for you.  
  
Gates is a leading manufacturer of application-specific fluid power and power transmission solutions. We push the boundaries of material science to engineer solutions that continually exceed customer expectations.  
  
Let's simplify it, think belts and hoses. Found in motorcycles, conveyor belts, cars, tractors, blenders, vacuum cleaners, bicycles, & 3D printers just to name a few. Because why not do it all? ## WHAT TO EXPECT

As an innovation leader, we look for ambitious, forward thinking, open-minded and well-rounded individuals to join our global team. Located in our Brandon, SD- Sioux Falls Metro plant, you will be a Quality Manager.

As the Quality Manager, this position provides leadership and direction for quality management across all phases of the manufacturing process, from raw materials to finished products. The role is responsible for guiding the site’s quality initiatives, ensuring product compliance, resolving customer and supplier quality concerns, and driving continuous improvement through root cause analysis and corrective actions.

As a key quality leader, this position works closely with plant leadership, cross-functional teams, customers, and suppliers to establish quality standards, strengthen processes, and improve overall performance.

## Key responsibilities (to name a few):

* Lead and execute quality improvement initiatives across manufacturing operations to improve product quality, reduce defects, and meet key performance goals.
* Oversee investigations and resolution of customer, warranty, and supplier quality issues using root cause analysis and corrective and preventive actions (CAPA).
* Partner with new product development and cross-functional teams to support Advanced Product Quality Planning (APQP), minimize quality risks, and ensure successful product launches.
* Manage the Production Part Approval Process (PPAP) to ensure accurate and timely product qualifications.
* Lead internal quality audits and Layered Process Audits (LPA) to ensure compliance and identify improvement opportunities.
* Collaborate with suppliers to resolve quality concerns, improve incoming material inspections, and strengthen supplier performance.
* Identify gaps in quality control processes and implement improvements to reduce defects, waste, and the Cost of Poor Quality.
* Maintain and continuously improve the site's Quality Management System (QMS), ensuring compliance with applicable standards, including ISO 9001, IATF 16949, and API Q1.
* Oversee quality-related change management activities to ensure changes are properly implemented, validated, and effective.
* Provide direct leadership, coaching, and development to Quality Technicians and Quality Auditors, including performance management and succession planning.
* Partner with plant leadership, operations, corporate quality, and cross-functional teams to drive quality performance and achieve business objectives.

## ABOUT YOU

* Bachelor’s degree required; Chemical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Physics, or a related technical field preferred
* 5 + years of experience in quality assurance manufacturing environment with 3 years of leadership or supervisory experience.
* Strong knowledge of automotive quality core tools, including APQP, PPAP, SPC, and MSA.
* Experience with quality problem-solving methodologies, including 5-Why, Fishbone Diagrams, Design of Experiments (DOE), and 8D.
* Strong leadership and interpersonal skills, with the ability to coach, develop, and motivate teams to achieve results.
* Results-oriented with strong organizational, analytical, and problem-solving skills.
* Experience with quality management and statistical analysis software, such as Minitab and SPC applications, preferred.
* Professional certifications, including Certified Quality Engineer (CQE), Certified Quality Manager (CQM), Certified Quality Auditor (CQA), or Six Sigma Black Belt - preferred
* Must be legally authorized to work in the United States without current or future company sponsorship.

## BENEFITS

    + Benefits begin on the first day of the month immediately following your date of hire
* Eligible for 3 weeks of paid vacation, additionally 8 sick days
* 11 paid holidays
* 401(k): company matching up to 6%
* Tuition Reimbursement
* Employee Discounts

**Job Description:**  
  
**Quality Manager**  
  
**Collaborate with Innovative 3Mers Around the World**  
  
Choosing where to start and grow your career has a major impact on your professional and personal life, so it's equally important you know that the company that you choose to work at, and its leaders, will support and guide you. With a wide variety of people, global locations, technologies and products, 3M is a place where you can collaborate with other curious, creative 3Mers.  
  
**This position provides an opportunity to transition from other private, public, government or military experience to a 3M career.**  
  
**The Impact You'll Make in this Role**  
  
The person hired for this position of Quality Manager will be responsible for providing quality leadership for operations and will be actively engaged in the development and execution of the plant quality strategies and tactics. These responsibilities will be directly tied to the global vision and algin with the long-term strategies of the plant operations. Key objectives will include developing a high-quality culture and team, delivering products with consistent and robust project quality, responding to customer complaints and driving effective and continuous improvement.  
  
As a Quality Manager, you will have the opportunity to tap into your curiosity and collaborate with some of the most innovative people around the world. Here, you will make an impact by:  
  
* Provides total quality management advice and consults with the plant leadership team to set short-term strategic direction and operating plans.
* Determines direction and priorities and assigns resources with full accountability for results of the quality functional area.
* Partners with engineering, operations, and customer service, to maintain and increase the quality level within the organization and to ensure product conformance to design data and design requirements.
* Drives reduction in complaints and cost of quality and regulatory standards.
* Furthers the plant's ability to advance quality at the source and utilize the technology resources to implement robust engineering controls that reduce human error.
* Direct oversight of the day-to-day FAA PMA operations within the facility and on-going monitoring and direct supervisor for those individuals appointed to issue Authorized Release Documents.

  
  
**Your Skills and Expertise**  
  
To set you up for success in this role from day one, 3M requires (at a minimum) the following qualifications:  
  
* Bachelor's degree or higher (completed and verified prior to start)

* Seven (7) years of plant quality and/or manufacturing operations experience working in a private, public, government or military environment
* Two (2) years of supervisory and/or managerial experience in a private, public, government or military environment.

  
  
Additional qualifications that could help you succeed even further in this role include:  
  
* Five (5) years of experience leading internal and external audits within the International Organization for Standardization (ISO).
* Demonstrated strong leadership ability and history of leading high-performance teams
* Demonstrated understanding of principle-based leadership and behaviors
* Experience in leading strategic and organizational development, operational excellence, lean implementation, financial accounting
* Effective communication skills
